subject: Technical lab session request — architecture & inference validation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Reese <morgan@averynet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: technical lab proposal & slot options

Hi Morgan —

Thanks again for the discovery call yesterday. Based on our notes it sounds like the right next step is a hands-on architecture lab focused on inference latency profiling, KV/prefix cache behavior, and deployment topology recommendations for Avery's multi-region pipelines.

Proposed format (90 minutes):
- 45 min: short architecture review + live run of a representative workload on a sandbox
- 30 min: interactive troubleshooting (SRE-style) and model/quantization tradeoffs
- 15 min: concrete next steps / mutual action items

Available slots (PT):
- Tue Apr 13, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Apr 14, 09:00–10:30
- Thu Apr 15, 13:00–14:30

Can you confirm which slot works for your team? Please tell me who from Avery will join (SRE, infra, security), and if there are any network/firewall constraints we should know about. I’ve cc’d Ben (solutions eng) and Laura (customer success) to help run the lab.

I’ll attach a short agenda and a checklist for sandbox access once we lock a time.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0197

--
Attachment: redwood_tech_lab_agenda_v1.pdf (agenda stub)

From: Morgan Reese <morgan@averynet.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@averynet.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: technical lab proposal & slot options

Hi Karthik —

Thanks — this looks great. The Avery infra team would like to include our SRE lead (Daniel) and our security engineer (Priya Patel) on the call. One ask: can you include a short section on our encryption-in-transit patterns and how Redwood integrates with our KMS?

Best slot for us right now is Wed Apr 14 but we have a scheduling conflict with one of our architects at 09:30 PT. If we can start 09:00 PT and keep to the 90 minute window we should be fine.

I’m attaching a small network constraints sheet that lists IP allowlists and proxy requirements.

Thanks,
Morgan Reese
Head of Platform, Avery Networks
morgan@averynet.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: technical lab proposal & slot options

Hi Morgan —

Awesome, thanks for the quick reply and for attaching the network sheet. We’ll add an explicit KMS/in-transit encryption primer to the agenda.

Confirming Wed Apr 14, 09:00–10:30 PT: I’ve created a provisional calendar invite here: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-inference-tech-lab-avery (I’ll update the link once we finalize).

Finalized agenda (attached):
- 09:00–09:15: Introductions + goals (Karthik, Ben)
- 09:15–09:45: Architecture walkthrough — routing, KV cache, batching patterns (Laura / Karthik)
- 09:45–10:15: Live sandbox run (sample workload) — latency & quantization tradeoffs (Ben)
- 10:15–10:30: Q&A and next steps

Attendees from Redwood: Karthik, Ben, Laura. Please invite Daniel and Priya on your side. If anything changes, let me know — otherwise I’ll circulate the updated agenda and the sandbox access instructions later today.

Thanks,
Karthik

--

Karthik —

Quick update: our lead architect just got pulled onto a priority incident and won’t be able to make Apr 14. Would you be able to move to Thu Apr 15 at 09:00 PT instead? Same duration and agenda — we really want Ben to run the sandbox while our SREs watch.

Apologies for the churn — we’ll make sure Daniel and Priya are on the updated invite.

Morgan

Thanks for the heads up — Thu Apr 15, 09:00–10:30 PT works for us. I’ve updated the invite and added Priya and Daniel to the attendee list. Updated calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-inference-tech-lab-avery

I’ve also attached a short sandbox access checklist and a KMS integration primer so your security engineer can scan ahead. If you can confirm the IP ranges from your network sheet are whitelisted for the session, we’ll provision the sandbox today.

See you Thursday — looking forward to the hands-on run.

Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference
